page: Amazon Web Services x8i.12xlarge is an eighth-generation memory-optimized instance built on the Nitro Hypervisor. It is powered by a dedicated 24-core, 48-vCPU Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at a sustained clock speed of 3.9 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system integrates 480 MB of shared L3 cache and supports Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) alongside AVX-512 vector instruction sets. Memory capacity reaches 768.0 GB of high-frequency DDR5 running at 7 GHz, delivering an allocation of 16.0 GB of system memory per vCPU.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong throughput across data-intensive tasks. The platform achieves 90.13 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and a score of 22,611.51 in PassMark database benchmarks. Cached memory bandwidth tops 3,831.46 GB/sec in small 16 KB read blocks, though uncached large-block throughput drops to 172.41 GB/sec for reads and 73.25 GB/sec for writes. Single-threaded gzip compression registers at 34.11 GB/sec, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 339.1 GB/sec. General multi-core processing delivers solid results with a Geekbench multi-core score of 19,574 and a PassMark CPU score of 69,147.78.

A key architectural consideration is the lack of bundled local NVMe storage, meaning all persistent data volumes must operate remotely across the 22 Gbps baseline network link. Additionally, while the server contains no discrete GPU accelerators, its AMX and AVX-512 hardware extensions assist CPU-based ML workloads, reaching 29.97 tokens/sec on 70B model prompt ingestion. The 16:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio offers favorable infrastructure efficiency for core-licensed, memory-bound enterprise software, reducing licensing footprints relative to raw RAM volume. The instance is suited for large in-memory key-value databases, SAP HANA, memory-heavy ETL processing, and enterprise database serving.
